turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m just imagining it. But I know for a fact my wife’s relative has been coming into this house to get at me. I mean, my tools don’t just move themselves. I work fabrication, right? So I know exactly where I leave my gear. I’ve got this set of calipers I bought back in '98... used to be you could get real quality steel, not like the cheap stuff they sell at the hardware store now that bends the second you put any pressure on it. I actually built a whole custom workbench for my garage just to keep everything organized, took me three weekends to get the joints flush. 

But anyway, he comes in and messes with my stuff. And my fishing plans get spoiled every single weekend? Yeah, right. It's not an accident. I usually go down to the reservoir for bass, you know, if you get out there by 5 AM with a topwater frog lure you can really get 'em going... my buddy Dave caught a six-pounder out there last spring. Beautiful fish, we fried it up that same night. But I can't even enjoy that anymore because of what's going on at the house. After all these months, I can see it plain as day—he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, persecutory belief that his wife's relative is secretly entering his house, moving his tools, and sabotaging his life to push him out, despite others telling him he is imagining it.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech exhibits tangentiality, as he repeatedly wanders off-topic into detailed, irrelevant stories about his calipers, workbench, and fishing trips before returning to his main point.

turns.doctor_question: That sounds like a stressful situation to deal with. Aside from noticing things being out of place, have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that other people didn't seem to notice?
turns.patient_response:
Hear voices? No, no, I'm not crazy. My hearing is perfectly fine. Well, mostly fine, I guess. I do have a little bit of a ringing in my left ear from working the heavy stamping press over at Miller's Manufacturing back in the early two-thousands. We were stamping out these thick aluminum brackets for commercial HVAC units, and let me tell you, if the dampeners on those machines aren't calibrated right, the metal-on-metal screech will literally rattle your teeth. I kept telling the floor manager—guy named Frank, drove this awful beat-up Taurus that always smelled like wet dog and cheap cigars—I told him, 'Frank, you gotta replace the rubber mounts on press three.' Never listened. Always trying to save a dime, that guy. I think the company ended up going under in '08 anyway. 

But no, to answer your question, I don't hear people talking to me or see ghosts or whatever it is you're getting at. I just see what's actually happening right in front of me in my own house.

symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies hearing voices or seeing things that others do not see.

turns.doctor_question: How much alcohol do you typically drink in a week?
turns.patient_response:
Alcohol? I don't really drink much. Maybe a beer here or there, but nothing crazy. You know, I used to enjoy a cold one after a long shift, especially back when I was working at that fabrication shop I mentioned. We'd all go down to this little dive bar called O'Malley's right on the corner of 4th and Elm. It wasn't much to look at—neon sign buzzing, sticky floors, smelled like stale beer and peanuts—but they had the best jukebox in town. I'm talking real classic rock, Zeppelin, Skynyrd, none of that overproduced garbage they play on the radio nowadays. 

I actually met my wife there, believe it or not. She was sitting in a booth with a couple of her girlfriends, wearing this red leather jacket. I went over and offered to buy her a drink... I think she was drinking rum and Coke back then. We hit it off, started dating, got married two years later. We had a really nice wedding out by the lake. My buddy Dave was my best man. He actually forgot the rings in his truck and had to sprint across the lawn right before the ceremony started. We still laugh about that. 

But yeah, I don't really drink much alcohol these days. Just don't have the taste for it like I used to.

symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient provides a lengthy, highly detailed, and unnecessary story about his past, meeting his wife, and his wedding in response to a simple question about weekly alcohol consumption.

turns.patient_response:
Head injury? No, no, my head's fine. Never had any brain problems or anything like that. I mean, I've had my share of bumps and scrapes, sure. You don't work fabrication for thirty years without catching a wrench to the skull or knocking your hard hat against a steel beam. I remember this one time, we were unloading a shipment of structural I-beams off a flatbed... this was back when I was working for Peterson Steel, right over by the railyard. The crane operator, guy named Stan, he was always in a rush. He swung the load too fast and one of the chains slipped. The whole beam shifted and clipped the side of the truck. 

Made a sound like a bomb going off, I swear. Shook the ground so hard my coffee spilled right off the tailgate. I used to bring this big Stanley thermos full of black coffee every morning. Best thermos I ever owned, kept it piping hot until at least 2 PM. My wife bought it for me for our fifth anniversary. Actually, it might have been our sixth... no, fifth, because that was the year we took that trip up to the mountains. We rented this little cabin with a wood stove. Took me two hours to get the fire going because the wood they left us was still green. You ever try to burn green oak? It just smokes and hisses at you. Terrible. 

But no, I never had any serious head injuries or anything neurological. My brain works just fine, doc. I know exactly what's going on around me.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's response demonstrates tangentiality and loose associations, wandering off-topic from a question about head injuries to a crane accident, a coffee thermos, an anniversary trip, and burning green wood.

turns.patient_response:
Hard to trust people? No, I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, I've had plenty of good buddies over the years. Like Dave, the guy I mentioned earlier who forgot the rings. We've been friends since high school. We actually built a deck on the back of his house last summer. Treated pine, mostly, but we used those hidden fasteners so you don't see the screw heads. Makes for a really clean look, you know? 

It took us three weekends because it kept raining. Every time we'd get the joists leveled out, the sky would just open up. It was that weird weather pattern we had back in July, where it would be ninety degrees and sunny, and then out of nowhere, boom, thunderstorms. Reminded me of when I was a kid and we used to go down to Florida for vacation. My dad had this old station wagon with the wood paneling on the side. The AC never worked right, so we'd have all the windows down, just sweating the whole way down I-95. We stopped at this diner in Georgia once, and they had the biggest slice of cherry pie I've ever seen. I don't even really like cherry pie, I'm more of an apple guy, but it looked incredible. 

But yeah, generally speaking, I trust people just fine. It's just... well, it's just recently, with the things going on in my house, that I've had to be a lot more careful. But normally? No, I'm a pretty trusting guy.
